distanceCaveats: STF and BLT/Padjelanta use 23 km. OSM and cropped Naturkartan linework compute about 22.1 km. Preserve the official 23 km until route geometry is normalized and endpoint policy is reviewed.

difficulty.label: moderate remote mountain stage
officialClaims: STF calls the terrain relatively easy but identifies this as the longest Padjelantaleden stage.
Naturkartan describes varied surfaces, easy mountain moorland, grassy pastures, willow brush, wet stretches with boardwalks, easy wades, and a steep descent to Låddejåhkå.
keyHazards: Long 23 km hut-to-hut day with no road access.
Three suspension bridges around Varggá/Vuojatädno and possible easy wades.
Vierttjajågåsj near Låddejåhkå can become a meaningful ford after rain.
Open fell sections can be exposed to fog, rain, wind, and poor visibility.
Final approach to Låddejåhkå is steep in the southbound direction.

sections.name: Etapp 5: BLT Stáloluoktastugan - BLT Duottarstugan

distanceCaveats: high for 18 km official display; medium-high for approximately 17.8-18.2 km geometry after hut access offsets

fieldReports: FarFarFromHome reported the reverse Duottar-Stáloluokta day as 18 km in 5 hours 10 minutes on 2023-07-12.

Wikiloc 2024 marks the reverse segment as moderate and notes that bad weather can make navigation and footing harder.

difficulty.label: long exposed mountain stage; not officially graded
officialClaims: STF lists a 18 km stage and describes a route past Gieddávrre, Bållávrjåhkå, moorland, small lakes, and finally Duottar.
Naturkartan gives 19 km and 6-8 hours for the Stáloluokta-Duottar part and warns that water is scarce after Bållávrjåhkå.
BLT/Padjelanta cabin pages place the endpoints in a remote hut chain with no road access.
keyHazards: Long distance with sustained exposure to weather and limited shelter between hut sites.
Seasonal Bållávrjåhkå suspension bridge; installation/removal timing can affect early/late season travel.
Water is reported as scarce after Bållávrjåhkå until closer to Duottar, so water planning matters.
Two generally simple wades before Duottar are reported by field sources, but difficulty depends on weather and meltwater.
Wet boardwalks, willow/marsh sections, stony ground, mosquitoes/blackflies, and poor mobile coverage can slow travel.
Reindeer herding areas and the Gieddávrre calf-marking enclosure require care and distance.

difficulty.label: short exposed high-plateau stage; not officially graded
officialClaims: STF describes rocky terrain with small lakes and snow lingering near the highest point.

Naturkartan describes easy-walked ground across dry grass heath, meadow, exposed bedrock, one usually easy ford at Gårråjávrátja, the highest point of Padjelantaleden at about 960 m, and then descent toward Darreluoppal/Tarraluoppal.
BLT/Padjelanta cabin pages identify the endpoints as remote hut sites with no road access.
keyHazards: High exposed plateau and Padjelantaleden's highest point around 950-960 m.
Late-lying snow and rapidly changing spring/early-season snow and stream conditions.
Usually easy but condition-dependent ford at or near Gårråjávrátja.
Additional small stream crossings reported in field accounts, especially in reverse direction near Darreluoppal.
Poor visibility, wind, rain, slippery wet planks/boardwalks, boggy sections, mosquitoes, and limited shelter.
Darreluoppal is just inside Sarek National Park, so boundary/rule context matters.

routeType.directionForImport: Såmmarlappa/Sammarlappa to Tarrekaise, matching STF north-to-south section order
routeType.descriptionForApp: The stage continues south through Tarradalen from Såmmarlappa toward Tarrekaise. It is a short and mostly flat valley stage, but the walking can still be tiring because of stones, wet ground, long boardwalk sections, side streams, and dense birch vegetation. The route starts near the Tarraätno river, passes small bridges, sparse herb-rich birch forest, open wetland and heath, then reaches the Bádurgårsså ravine and alluvial fan where the Vaimok/Tarraälvshyddan side route leaves the Padjelantaleden. After the valley opens toward Tarraure, the stage ends at STF Tarrekaise on the lake's northern shore.

sections.name: Etapp 9: STF Tarrekaise Fjällstuga - STF Njunjes Fjällstuga

distanceCaveats: high for official contradiction; high for about 7.0 km from Naturkartan GPX; keep STF 6 km as the primary STF display claim until normalization policy decides otherwise

fieldReports: Roversmountains reported Tarrekaise-Njunjes in about 3 hours.
I-Trekkings reported over 2 hours for the 6 km Tarrekaise-Njunjes leg on 2006-08-03.
Komoot planning data gives 1 hour 53 minutes, but Naturkartan and field reports support keeping the official 2-4 hour planning range.

difficulty.description: No formal official grade found. Naturkartan describes the stage as short but strenuous, especially rocky and muddy in rain. Field reports repeatedly mention stones, mud, slippery duckboards, wet rock slabs, dense vegetation, and a steep rocky descent into Njunjes.

routeType.directionForImport: Tarrekaise to Njunjes, matching STF north-to-south section order and Naturkartan BD71 stored direction
routeType.descriptionForApp: A short but rough Tarradalen stage from Tarrekaise to Njunjes. The route leaves the Tarrekaise hut area through dense mountain birch and high vegetation, follows the north side of Tarraure and Luoppal with views toward Hilldo and Tarradalen, then climbs onto a more open plateau before a steep, rocky descent to STF Njunjes above Tarraätno. Wet weather can make the rocky ground, mud, boardwalks and descent noticeably slower than the distance suggests.

sections.name: Etapp 10: STF Njunjes Fjällstuga - STF Kvikkjokk Fjällstation
sections.to: STF Kvikkjokk Fjällstation via Bobäcken boat landing

distanceCaveats: high for 12 km walking plus 3 km boat; high for computed 12.3-12.5 km walking line; medium-high for 3.4 km OSM ferry/access line

fieldReports: I-Trekkings reported Njunjes-Kvikkjokk as 13 km in 2 hours 50 minutes in 2006, with boat needed after the walk.
Wikiloc 2016 lists Njunjes-Kvikkjokk as 12.39 km and 2 hours 35 minutes, likely the walking leg only.
Hikr 2008 reverse report lists Kvikkjokk-Njunjes as 12 km and 4 hours after boat to Bobäcken.
Route-app totals that include the boat/gateway leg list about 15.4-16.1 km and 3.5-4.1 hours.

difficulty.description: No formal official grade found. The walking is generally low-gradient forest trail, but official and field sources repeatedly flag wet/swampy ground, boardwalks, mosquitoes, bridges, rocky forest trail, monotonous conifer forest, and mud after rain. Treat as easy-to-moderate rather than purely easy, especially in wet or mosquito-heavy conditions.

routeType.type: point-to-point remote hut-to-gateway hiking stage with required boat/access transfer
routeType.directionForImport: Njunjes to Bobäcken for the hiking geometry, then Bobäcken to Kvikkjokk as boat/access connector
routeType.descriptionForApp: The final Padjelantaleden stage leaves STF Njunjes and descends through Tarradalen toward Kvikkjokk. The walking leg crosses wet ground, mixed forest, old hay meadows at Njunjes and Bäcken, the broad Njunjesjåhkå alluvial fan, rocky conifer forest, and bridges over Vallebäcken/Vállegårsså before reaching the wet, mosquito-prone forest and boat landing at Bobäcken. From Bobäcken the normal route requires a paid boat over Tarraätno/Gamájåhkå delta to Kvikkjokk, where STF Kvikkjokk Fjällstation provides lodging, food and transport connections.
